newsitem.title: USA: Sony sues U.S. firms over counterfeit games.
newsitem.headline: Sony sues U.S. firms over counterfeit games.

text.p: Sony Interactive Entertainment Inc. said Friday it filed several suits against U.S. and Canadian companies it accuses of selling counterfeit versions of its PlayStation video games.
The action comes after a recent amendment expanded the U.S. Racketeering Influenced and Corrupt Organisation Act to permit suits against groups dealing in pirated intellectual property.
Sony Interactive, a Foster City, Calif.-based subsidiary of Sony Corp. of America, said its lawsuits seek to impound infringing products in addition to recovery of damages.
"On behalf of the consumers that purchase the PlayStation and its games, we will go to any length to protect the integrity of our products," a spokesman said.

"We hope this suit sends a clear message that Sony will not tolerate illegal actions as they relate to our products and that we will vigorously prosecute all infringements to the greatest extent of the law."
The company said a coordinated litigation effort was taken against privately held companies based in New York, Toronto, Miami and Orange County in California.

Sony said one of the lawsuits charges that National Console Support and other companies have marketed a device that enables counterfeit games to operate on the PlayStation game console and therefore contributes to the infringement of copyrights and trademarks controlled by Sony.

It said companion suits filed simultaneously charge Super Collector and Video Games Plus with unlawfully selling and distributing counterfeit games in the United States via the Internet, electronic-mail, and the U.S. Mail.
Sony said counterfeits of its games, which are contained on compact discs, are easy to spot because it uses a unique process to colour its own discs black.

"To date, counterfeiters have been unable to duplicate this process," the company said in a statement. "If a consumer has a question about the legitimacy of a game, they should flip the disc over and look for the black back."
The company said consumers who find counterfeit games can call a special Sony hotline at 800 345-SONY.
